subject: new error with runMI: The number of convergent replications is less than or equal to 1.

messages.author: e2384f4a7834b679
messages.subject: new error with runMI: The number of convergent replications is less than or equal to 1.
parts:
Hello everyone,

Following the good advice given to me in this thread https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/lavaan/R1K2KKINygI I managed to get my sem-models to work.

However, it seems version 0.4-5 has brought with it another problem. One of my CFA models that used to work in 0.4 now produce this error:

     1. Convergence 2. Proper SE 3. Proper Variance Estimate Used for pooling
[1,]           TRUE         TRUE                       FALSE            FALSE
[2,]           TRUE         TRUE                       FALSE            FALSE
[3,]           TRUE         TRUE                        TRUE             TRUE
[4,]           TRUE         TRUE                       FALSE            FALSE
[5,]           TRUE         TRUE                       FALSE            FALSE
Error in runMI(cfa.oid.model4, data = mice.imp, fun = "cfa", std.lv = F,  :
  Please increase the number of imputations. The number of convergent replications is less than or equal to 1. See the details above.

The script looks like this:
cfa.oid.model4<-'
    oit =~ oit1 + oit2 + oit3 + oit4
    oce =~ oce1 + oce2 + oce3 + oce4
    oia =~ oia1 + oia2 + oia3 + oia4

    oce1 ~~ oce3 + oce4
    oce2 ~~ oce3
    oce2 ~~ oce4
    oit3 ~~ oit4
    oia1 ~~ oia4
    oia2 ~~ oia3
'

cfa.oid.sem.nf3.4<-runMI(cfa.oid.model4, data = mice.imp, fun = "cfa", std.lv = F, estimator = "WLSMV")

I wonder if it was v 0.4 that was buggy and allowed the analysis to complete or if a bug has been introduced in 0.4-5?

Thanks for any help you may provide.


Best regards,
Mikkel

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: new error with runMI: The number of convergent replications is less than or equal to 1.
parts:
Hi Mikkel,

I'm not sure I would quantify this as a "bug" in either version, it is more of a philosophical switch. This error only occurs when either 0 or 1 of the imputed data sets produce a model that converges. When 0 of the models converge there are not results to view so the error makes sense. With 1 model converged there are "results" (which were reported in earlier versions) but they aren't the results from multiple imputation. Instead they are based on a single imputation (so no pooling needs to be done). runMI provides you with the imputed data set that did converge (in your case #3) so if you wanted to see the results from that data set you could use the cfa command in lavaan on only that imputed data set. I wouldn't recommend drawing too many conclusions from a single imputation (hence the warning) but it might be useful to diagnose specific issues with the model (especially in this case where it seems like the other imputed data sets are giving you improper estimates of variances).

Alex

Hi Alex,

Thank you for the explanation. I think that is a really good move. It defies the purpose of multiple imputation to only analyse one dataset (thinking that the analysis is actually pooled across the m multiply imputed datasets), so definately an improvement :).


Best regards,
Mikkel
